title: Chola naval expedition against Srivijaya
summary: In 1025 the Chola king Rajendra I sent a naval fleet against the maritime power Srivijaya. One scholarly account has it crossing to Sumatra's west coast, sailing south into the Sunda Strait and first raiding Palembang, where the Srivijayan king was captured; the Cholas looted rather than occupied, leaving Srivijaya weakened.

uncertainty.note: Cambridge University Press's chapter summaries and Encyclopedia.com give 1025 for the raid; the journal paper also gives 1025 and notes an earlier raid in 1017 (Cambridge). Individual stops are not dated on any opened page, so the path carries no waypoint years.

where.modern_name: Barus and Palembang, Sumatra, Indonesia, by way of the Sunda Strait
where.historical_name: Srivijaya, a maritime power based on Sumatra, attacked by the fleet of the Chola empire of southern India

waypoints.label: Barus on the west coast of North Sumatra, a port the paper says supplied the fleet after the Indian Ocean crossing.
Sunda Strait, which the fleet sailed into after passing south along the Sumatran west coast.
Palembang, the first Srivijayan city raided according to the paper, where the king was taken.

importance.justification: A rare overseas naval campaign by an Indian state, which struck the power that controlled the Malacca and Sunda straits.

related.because: The raid sacked Palembang and captured the Srivijayan king, weakening its dominance of the straits.

beats.caption: Rajendra's fleet crosses the Indian Ocean to Sumatra's west coast, resupplies at Barus, and sails south toward the Sunda Strait.
The fleet takes Srivijaya by surprise and raids Palembang first, sacking the palace and capturing King Sangrama Vijayottunggavarman.
The Cholas loot Srivijayan cities without taking over their administration, leaving the Srivijaya network weakened.

reviewer_note: Least sure: the route (Barus, Sunda Strait, Palembang) rests on one journal paper that itself cites other works; Kedah/Kadaram is left off because no opened page orders it in the route. The cause of the campaign is disputed on the pages and is not stated here. Wikidata points are centres of a district, strait and city.
